title: Zesty Irish Salmon Soup
description: A citrusy, comforting Irish soup that pairs tender sous‑vide salmon with fresh lemon zest, bright herbs, and a light, savory broth.
instructions: Set the sous‑vide water bath to 125°F (51°C). Place the salmon fillets in a vacuum‑sealed bag with a pinch of sea salt, black pepper, and the chopped dill. Seal the bag and cook for 30–45 minutes.
While the salmon is cooking, heat the coconut oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the diced carrots, celery, and onion to the pot. Sauté until the vegetables are softened, about 5 minutes.
Pour in the water, bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, and let it reduce slightly for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped kale, sea salt, and black pepper to the pot. Simmer until the kale is wilted, about 3–4 minutes.
Remove the pot from the heat and set aside.
Take the salmon out of the sous‑vide bag, pat it dry, and crumble it into bite‑size pieces.
Return the salmon to the pot, gently stir, and add the lemon zest and lemon juice.
Taste the soup and adjust seasoning with additional salt or pepper if needed. Warm the soup through for 2 minutes.
Ladle the soup into bowls, garnish with extra dill if desired, and serve hot.
